reviewType: Assistant editorial review using trusted nursing texts, clinical guidance, and product information
independentClinicianApproval: Pending; this editorial and software review is not a professional clinical sign-off or a guarantee that the bank is error-free.
method: Read every active legacy five-part case and seven-part clinical blueprint, including its assessment, action, teaching, safety, planning, evaluation, and reasoning claims as applicable.
Compared clinical principles with the cited Open RN nursing chapters and focused primary guidance. Replaced broad or misplaced references where a more direct supporting source was identified.

Expanded alternative explanations with the alternative clinical context and rationale, followed by the rationale for the present case; an alternative can be appropriate elsewhere without being the best answer here.

Visually checked the WHO IMCI chart booklet printed pages 1, 2, 3, 5, and 6 (PDF pages 5, 6, 7, 9, and 10): danger signs, age-specific breathing thresholds, dehydration and persistent diarrhea, mastoiditis, and nutritional edema.
Screened exact normalized stems and clinical similarity. Replaced five close overlaps using fresh IDs; kept distinct disorders or decisions that share terminology.
Verified all previously stored answer indices and peer identities against publication snapshots. Documented clinical wording clarifications do not reshuffle saved choices.
sourceFamilies: Open Resources for Nursing via the official NLM Bookshelf/Open RN texts
WHO IMCI, disease guidance, and maternal guidance
RCH, Queensland Health, NHS and other health-system clinical guidance
NIH institutes, NCI, NIDDK, NEI and NIA
Professional society guidance including UKKA, Endocrine Society, ICS and AASLD

focusedCorrections.description: Counts include reference improvements and clinical context or explanation changes; they are not counts of previously wrong answer keys.

duplicateReview.sharedCaseVignettes: Intentional: linked items use different nursing-process objectives.

retainedSimilarPairs.reason: Postpartum uterine infection and intraamniotic infection during labor differ in timing and maternal-fetal assessment.
Different primary acid-base disorders and causes; values and response priorities differ.
Routine protection of a functioning access differs from urgent assessment of an absent thrill.
Potassium-related risk and a hemodynamically unstable tachyarrhythmia require different focused review.
Renal perfusion assessment and measurement/replacement of high ileostomy output have different specific care needs.
Dengue warning signs and pregnancy warning-sign counseling are distinct clinical settings.
Infection-related organ dysfunction and hemorrhagic shock require cause-specific treatment.
A mechanical catheter problem differs from a hypertensive spinal-cord emergency with a bladder trigger.
Possible rupture and possible intraamniotic infection have different findings and emergency pathways.
General unanswered consent questions differ from a language-access problem requiring a qualified interpreter.
Vesicant chemotherapy management differs from vasoactive extravasation with a simultaneous need to maintain lifesaving circulatory support.
Febrile-child seizure assessment and adult generalized seizure safety have age- and cause-specific context.
Chest-drain respiratory deterioration and catheter-triggered dysreflexia involve distinct devices, physiology and priorities.

referenceAvailability.caution: HTTP success, source-title matching, and lexical passage retrieval do not establish clinical correctness. Access-restricted sources were also consulted through focused public source excerpts or official document retrieval where available.
